title: Consensus that images are somehow to be cultivated and adored—yet Schoolmen still quarrel over the mode and nature of that cult
source_text: XXXV. Sed quanquam Scholae Romanae Theologi communi consensu agnoscant imagines, aliquo saltem modo, colendas & adorandas esse, adeoque pium & laudabile esse, ipsas devote osculari, thus ipsis adolere, luminaria accendere & coram eis genu flectere, sive procumbere, minime tamen inter se consentiunt quae & qualis istius cultus ratio atque natura sit. Quod observat Vasquez tomi jam allegati disput. 108. cap. 1. Cum Catholici omnes, inquit, contra Iconomachos in aliquo cultu & adoratione imaginibus deferenda facile conveniant, variant in modo seu ipsa natura adorationis.
pass_a_gloss: But although the Theologians of the Roman School by common consensus acknowledge that images are, at least in some way, to be cultivated and adored, and so that it is pious and praiseworthy devoutly to kiss them, to burn incense to them, to light lights and to bend the knee or prostrate before them, yet they by no means agree among themselves what and of what sort the reason and nature of that cult is. Which Vasquez observes in disput. 108, ch. 1 of the tome already cited: Although all Catholics, he says, easily agree against the Iconomachs in some cult and adoration to be paid to images, they vary in the mode or in the very nature of the adoration.
pass_b_english: Roman Schoolmen agree images somehow deserve kiss, incense, lights, and kneeling.
They still split on the mode and nature of that cult—Vasquez: unity against iconomachs, diversity on how adoration works.

lemmas.latin: variant in modo seu ipsa natura
lemmas.gloss: they vary in the mode or in the very nature

choices.why: Closes the Councils/praxis block; opens the School dispute for XXXVI+.
